lines: Oh! A visitor. Nobody visits. I mostly stand near the well and think about bread.
dialogues.challenge: Want to come think about bread at my base?
dialogues.accept: Only if I win! Or lose! I'm flexible!

lines: I don't have a job yet. I'm keeping my options open.
What could you do at a base?
Carry things! Farm a bit! Look busy when you walk past!
dialogues.challenge: Prove it in a fight and you're hired.
dialogues.accept: Ooh, a job interview. With punching.

lines: Can I tell you a secret? Zombies terrify me. They're just like us, but worse at conversation.
dialogues.challenge: I'll protect you, if you can hold your own.
dialogues.accept: Deal! Hold my... well, nothing. Let's go.

lines: If I could live anywhere, it'd be a flower forest. Bees, blossoms, no creepers sneaking up on you.
That's what they want you to think.
dialogues.challenge: I know a base with flowers. Fight me for a spot?
dialogues.accept: For flowers? Absolutely.

lines: My grandmother said the world was made by twelve dragons, and that one day the First would wake again.
She was right about the weather every single time. So... yes?
dialogues.challenge: Let's see if you've got some dragon fire in you.
dialogues.accept: My grandmother would be so proud. Or horrified.
dialogues.farewell: She'll want to know you were polite.

lines: Up before the sun, wheat, carrots, potatoes, repeat. You'd think the chickens would say thank you.
They lay eggs at me. I choose to see it as gratitude.
dialogues.challenge: Come farm for me. After a little fight.
dialogues.accept: Ha! I've wrestled pumpkins bigger than you.

lines: At a base, I'd keep your fields planted and harvested. You'd never go hungry again.
Especially the hard stuff. Beetroot fears me.
dialogues.challenge: Sounds perfect. Fight me for it?
dialogues.accept: Roll up your sleeves, then!
dialogues.decline: Maybe when I have more fields.

lines: You know what keeps me up at night? Ravagers. Great big beasts trampling through the crops.
And they never even eat the wheat. Just ruin it. Rude.
dialogues.challenge: I'll keep the ravagers off your fields.
dialogues.accept: Show me you can handle a ravager. Starting with me!
dialogues.farewell: Keep an eye on the treeline.

lines: Plains, plains, plains. Flat ground, good soil, sky as far as you can see.
Boring is just peaceful with a bad attitude.
dialogues.challenge: My base has wide open fields.
dialogues.accept: Now you're speaking my language. Let's go!
dialogues.farewell: It's the best one in Serantia.

lines: They say Mokele-mbembe spread the first forests and grass across the world. Every seed I plant is a little piece of its work.
You think about that while farming?
Every row. Makes the back ache a little less.
dialogues.challenge: Bring that thinking to my base.
dialogues.accept: Then let's settle it the old-fashioned way!

lines: Sat by this river since dawn. Caught two cod, one boot and a saddle.
Don't ask me how. The river provides.
dialogues.challenge: Fish for me instead. After we fight.
dialogues.accept: Reel me in, if you can!
dialogues.decline: Hope the river gives you something good.

lines: Put me by some water at your base and I'll keep the fish coming. Treasure too, if the river's feeling generous.
Enchanted books, name tags... once a whole bow!
dialogues.challenge: I need a fisherman. Let's do this.
dialogues.accept: Hook, line and sinker. Come on!

lines: Drowned. Can't stand them. Something about a soggy fellow throwing tridents at you.
And they always smell like old seaweed.
dialogues.challenge: My base is drowned-free. Fight for a spot?
dialogues.accept: Then cast your line at me!
dialogues.farewell: Never turn your back on a river.

lines: Give me a warm ocean, coral reefs, turtles drifting by. That's paradise.
I tried a frozen ocean once. My beard froze to my rod.
dialogues.challenge: My base has a nice warm pond.
dialogues.accept: Warm water? Now you've got me. Let's fight!
dialogues.farewell: Wave at the turtles for me.

lines: My father said Gargouille filled the world's hollows with water, and the deep remembers everything the land forgets.
Sunken kingdoms. Old crowns. I've hooked a few things I put right back.
dialogues.challenge: Come tell me more at my base.
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you're as strong as the tide!
dialogues.farewell: The water certainly keeps its own.

lines: Tracked a fox for two days. It stole my lunch, then my boot, then my dignity.
We have an understanding now. It keeps the boot.
dialogues.challenge: Hunt for me. After a duel.
dialogues.accept: Ha! You'll be quicker than the fox, I hope.

lines: At your base I'd keep bows strung, arrows fletched, and the best drops from every creature I come across.
Rule one: never trust anything that rustles.
dialogues.challenge: Rule two: fight me.
dialogues.accept: Rule two accepted! Draw!

lines: Everyone thinks hunters are fearless. Spiders. Big ones. Climbing walls. Nope.
You hunt monsters but fear spiders?
They have eight legs. Eight! Nobody needs that many.
dialogues.challenge: No spiders at my base. Promise.
dialogues.accept: I'll hold you to that. Let's go!

lines: Old growth taiga. Tall spruce, cold air, wolves howling in the distance. That's home.
Wolves are fine. They don't have eight legs.
dialogues.challenge: My base has spruce trees.
dialogues.accept: Then I'm already half sold. Fight me!
dialogues.farewell: Mind the wolves. Pet them, though.

lines: Hunters remember the old story: the Lindworm made the plain beasts, the deer and wolves and rabbits, and gave them freedom.
To be just what they are. I respect that. I try to hunt the same way.
dialogues.challenge: Hunt beside me, then.
dialogues.accept: Show me you've got the instincts!

lines: Shh! ... Oh, sorry. Force of habit. I shush the chickens too.
Never. Chickens have no respect for literature.
dialogues.challenge: Read for me at my base. After a duel.
dialogues.accept: A duel! How thrillingly unscholarly. Very well!

lines: Give me a desk at your base and I'll keep the shelves stocked: books, paper, even an enchanted volume or two.
I can certainly lose them in a very organised way.
dialogues.challenge: Organised loss sounds great. Fight me?
dialogues.accept: Footnotes at dawn!

lines: The Endermen. They pick up blocks. From my library. And never put them back.
Last week it was a whole bookshelf. Overdue forever.
dialogues.challenge: My base has no Endermen. Fight for a spot?
dialogues.accept: An Enderman-free library? Let's go!
dialogues.decline: Don't look them in the eye.

lines: A snowy village, a crackling fire, a stack of books nobody else has read. Bliss.
That's what the fire's for. And the books. Mostly the books.
dialogues.challenge: I'll build you a cosy reading nook.
dialogues.accept: With a fireplace? Sold. En garde!

lines: Our oldest records speak of the Age of Ashes, when kingdoms reached too far and the world burned for it.
Do the books say how it started?
Every book says something different. That's what worries me.
dialogues.challenge: Help me make sure it doesn't happen again.
dialogues.accept: Then let's begin with a lesson in combat!

lines: Just got back from the edge of the map. Turns out the map just... keeps going.
Wherever the compass doesn't point. It's always wrong anyway.
dialogues.challenge: Explore from my base. After a fight.
dialogues.accept: Ha! I've fought sand storms. Bring it!
dialogues.farewell: If you see my hat, it's mine.

lines: At your base I'd keep maps and compasses on hand, plus all the odd keepsakes I bring home: discs, trims, sherds.
Broken pottery. Very important. Don't ask why.
dialogues.challenge: I'll take the pottery. Fight me?
dialogues.accept: For science! And pottery!
dialogues.farewell: The ruins will wait for us.

lines: I've crossed deserts and jungles, but the Warden? Down in the deep dark? Absolutely not.
I've heard it. That was plenty. My ears are still sorry.
dialogues.challenge: No Wardens at my base. Fight for a room?
dialogues.accept: A safe bed after all this? Let's go!

lines: Badlands! Red rock, gold in the hills, and sunsets that look like the sky's on fire.
dialogues.challenge: My base has a lovely view too.
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you're worth the trip!

lines: I've found ruins older than any kingdom: roads that lead nowhere, towers broken in half. The First Dragon's watchposts, some say.
If anyone could do it, it'd be someone crazy enough to try. Like you.
dialogues.challenge: Then come help me rebuild them.
dialogues.accept: Prove you've got the guts first!

lines: Hammer, anvil, sparks, burnt eyebrows. That's my morning.
My eyebrows gave up years ago.
dialogues.challenge: Forge for me. After a scrap.
dialogues.accept: A scrap! Now you're speaking my metal.
dialogues.farewell: Too late. Never too late. Ow.

lines: At a base I'd keep ores sorted and smelted, and turn out tools, weapons and armor. And I'll sharpen your blade, if you've got the XP.
Plus five. Sharp enough to cut a cloud.
dialogues.challenge: Sharpen me something now. Fight first.
dialogues.accept: Steel on steel! Come on!

lines: Silverfish. You mine one block and suddenly the whole wall is wriggling.
Tiny and LOTS. Size doesn't matter when it's everywhere.
dialogues.challenge: My walls are silverfish-free.
dialogues.accept: Then I'm hammering my way in!

lines: Mountains. Iron in the cliffs, coal in the seams, snow on the peaks to cool my hammer.
Everything near me gets hot. It's a gift.
dialogues.challenge: My base sits on good ore.
dialogues.accept: Then let's see who's harder: you or the iron!

lines: Fafnir laid the mineral veins we mine, they say. Every ingot I forge is a little piece of the world's bones.
Fire and poetry aren't so different. Both make things glow.
dialogues.challenge: Forge something great with me.
dialogues.accept: Then let's forge a fight first!
dialogues.farewell: The world's bones are in good hands.

lines: Cut stone all day. Stacked it. Unstacked it. Stacked it again, but straighter.
Because the first stack offended me.
dialogues.challenge: Build for me. After a fight.
dialogues.accept: Solid choice. Stand firm!
dialogues.farewell: Straight lines, friend. Always straight lines.

lines: At a base I'd keep you in stone, bricks, terracotta, concrete, glass, even ice. Name a block, I've got a pile.
Any block. Except dirt. I have standards.
dialogues.challenge: No dirt. Deal. Fight me?
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you're built to last!

lines: Creepers. Wait, no, there aren't any here. Then Ravagers. They knock down WALLS.
Every wall is my wall, emotionally.
dialogues.challenge: My walls are ravager-proof. Mostly.
dialogues.accept: Mostly? Let me fix that. After I fight you!

lines: Stony shores. Grey stone, grey sea, grey sky. Perfectly balanced.
Grey is the colour of reliability.
dialogues.challenge: My base needs some reliable stone.
dialogues.accept: Then let's lay the first block: you!

lines: When the Age of Ashes ended, masons rebuilt what was left. My family's been patching up Serantia ever since.
Ten thousand years of patches. The world's mostly mortar now.
dialogues.challenge: Help me patch it up some more.
dialogues.accept: Then let's see if you're sturdy enough!

lines: Measure twice, cut once. Then measure again, because I forgot what I cut.
dialogues.challenge: Build with me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Sawdust and fisticuffs! Let's go!

lines: Put me to work at your base and you'll never run short of logs, planks, doors, fences, anything made of wood.
I prefer to think of it as giving trees a new career.
dialogues.challenge: My trees need new careers. Fight me?
dialogues.accept: Timber! I mean, en garde!
dialogues.farewell: The trees will wait. They're good at that.

lines: Termites. Do we have termites? I don't know. That's what scares me.
dialogues.challenge: My base is termite-free. I think.
dialogues.accept: You think? I'll inspect it personally. After we fight!

lines: Dark oak forests. Giant trees, mushroom shade, wood as far as the eye can see.
It's cosy. Gloomy is just cosy without a fireplace.
dialogues.challenge: My base has a fireplace.
dialogues.accept: Fireplace AND wood? Let's go!

lines: Old stories say Mokele-mbembe raised the first forests, and every tree since is a cousin of those.
Do you feel bad chopping them?
I always plant two for every one. Family is family.
dialogues.challenge: Plant some at my base.
dialogues.accept: Two for one! But first, one fight!

lines: Breakfast, lunch, dinner, second dinner. Somebody's always hungry.
Me. The chef must taste everything.
dialogues.challenge: Cook for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: A fight before dinner works up an appetite!

lines: At a base I'd keep the kitchen running: cooked meat, cakes, pies, stews. You'll never fight hungry.
Every day is somebody's birthday, if you believe hard enough.
dialogues.challenge: I believe. Fight me?
dialogues.accept: Then let's stir things up!

lines: Phantoms. You stay up late baking one night and suddenly there's screeching from the sky.
They come when you don't sleep.
So now I bake in the morning. I'm terrible in the morning.
dialogues.challenge: My base has a bed for you.
dialogues.accept: A bed AND a kitchen? Let's go!

lines: Savanna! Warm, sunny, perfect for drying herbs and roasting things over an open fire.
Cooking outside is just a kitchen with a better ceiling.
dialogues.challenge: My base has a big sky too.
dialogues.accept: Then let's fire up the grill. Starting with you!

lines: Y Ddraig Goch breathed the first flame into the world. Every fire I cook on owes it a little thanks.
Every time something doesn't burn. So... rarely.
dialogues.challenge: Bring that fire to my base.
dialogues.accept: Then let's turn up the heat!

lines: Stitch, tan, stitch, tan. My fingers have more holes than my aprons.
Leather's tough. So am I. Mostly my fingers.
dialogues.challenge: Stitch for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Let's see if your hide's as tough as mine!

lines: Bring me to your base and I'll keep you in leather, armor, saddles, harnesses and leads. Mounts will love you.
If it has a back, I can make it a saddle.
dialogues.challenge: Saddle up. After we fight.
dialogues.accept: Ha! Giddy up, then!

lines: Hoglins. Big snorting pig-monsters that charge at you for no reason.
I make leather. They think I'm... recruiting.
dialogues.challenge: No hoglins at my base.
dialogues.accept: Then I'm already interested. Let's fight!
dialogues.farewell: Every pig in it holds a grudge.

lines: Meadows. Cows grazing, horses running, flowers everywhere. A leatherworker's dream.
Isn't that a bit sad, for the cows?
I give them names first. It's respectful.
dialogues.challenge: I've got a meadow at my base.
dialogues.accept: Then lead me there. After a fight!

lines: The Lindworm gave us the plain beasts, the cows and horses, so we could live alongside them. My trade honours that gift.
Especially the leather. Nothing wasted, nothing forgotten.
dialogues.challenge: Honour it at my base.
dialogues.accept: Then prove yourself worthy of the work!

lines: Watered the roses, trimmed the hedges, talked to the tulips. They're very good listeners.
dialogues.challenge: Garden for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you've got a green thumb... and a strong fist!

lines: At a base I'll keep everything growing: saplings, flowers, moss, grass. Your crops will shoot up like they're late for something.
Faster everything. Plants just like me.
dialogues.challenge: My plants need you. Fight?
dialogues.accept: Then let's grow some muscles!
dialogues.farewell: Your garden will miss me already.

lines: Sheep. They eat EVERYTHING. I planted a whole flower bed and a sheep ate it in one afternoon.
dialogues.challenge: I'll keep the sheep away from you.
dialogues.accept: A sheep-free garden? I'm in. Fight me!

lines: Cherry groves! Pink petals drifting down like snow. Best smell in the world.
dialogues.challenge: I'll plant cherry trees at my base.
dialogues.accept: Pink petals AND a fight? Let's go!

lines: The Fairy Dragon, they say, made the enchanted groves where flowers glow and time moves strangely. I've found one. Once.
I was there ten minutes. I came out a week later. My tomatoes were furious.
dialogues.challenge: Help me find one again.
dialogues.accept: Prove you can handle the Fae first!

lines: Spun wool, dyed it blue, dyed it green, dyed myself purple by accident.
Is that why your hands are purple?
It's a look. I'm making it a look.
dialogues.challenge: Weave for me. After a fight?
dialogues.accept: Let's tangle, then!

lines: At your base I'll keep wool, carpets, beds, banners and dyes coming. Everything warm and colourful.
I'll make you a banner so grand the goblins will want to frame it.
dialogues.challenge: Make me a banner. Fight first.
dialogues.accept: A battle banner, then! En garde!

lines: Moths! Do you have moths? Tell me you don't have moths.
Think isn't good enough with moths.
dialogues.challenge: My base is moth-free. Fight for a loom?
dialogues.accept: Then let's go before the moths find out!

lines: Snowy plains. Everyone needs a scarf. Business is booming.
Not if you're wearing six of my scarves.
dialogues.challenge: My base could use some scarves.
dialogues.accept: Then I'll knit after I win!

lines: The old weavers say Ladon wove magic through the world like thread, and if you pull the right one, everything changes.
I pulled one on my sleeve once. Unravelled the whole thing.
dialogues.challenge: Let's pull some threads together.
dialogues.accept: Then let's start with a fight!

lines: Built a machine that sorts my socks. Now I can't find any socks.
The machine has them. It won't say where.
dialogues.challenge: Build for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Let's test your mechanics!

lines: Give me a corner of your base and I'll keep the redstone humming, the rails laid and the minecarts rolling.
I can automate your farm, your door and probably your breakfast.
dialogues.challenge: Automate this: a fight.
dialogues.accept: Initiating combat protocol!

lines: Lightning. One bolt in the wrong place and my whole contraption goes up in sparks.
Have you tried a lightning rod?
I've tried six. The lightning finds them rude.
dialogues.challenge: My base has plenty of lightning rods.
dialogues.accept: Then let's spark something!

lines: Lush caves! Glow berries for lighting, clay for parts, and dripleaf for testing gravity.
It still works. I checked. Several times.
dialogues.challenge: My base has caves nearby.
dialogues.accept: Then let's run an experiment. On you!

lines: Piasa made the storms, they say. Lightning, wind, thunder. I just try to bottle a little of that power for redstone.
Hard to say. My workshop gets struck a suspicious amount.
dialogues.challenge: Bring that storm to my base.
dialogues.accept: Then let's make some thunder!

lines: Mixed two potions this morning. Turned my left ear green.
The right one's turning invisible. Very slowly.
dialogues.challenge: Brew for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: An experiment in combat! How exciting!

lines: At your base I'll keep the brewing stands bubbling: healing, speed, strength, whatever you need.
Night vision, water breathing, and one that makes you smell like flowers. Unintentionally.
dialogues.challenge: I'll take the flowers. Fight me?
dialogues.accept: Shake well before fighting!

lines: Witches. They're my competition. And they cheat. Throwing potions at people is not how you sell them.
dialogues.challenge: No witches at my base. Just you.
dialogues.accept: A monopoly! I love it. Fight me!

lines: Swamps! Slime, mushrooms, mysterious bubbles. Every ingredient a brewer could want.
dialogues.challenge: My base has a swamp nearby.
dialogues.accept: Then let's stir things up!

lines: Ladon, the Dragon of Arcane, wrote the rules magic follows. Every potion I make bends one just a little.
Not even slightly. That's how you know it's working.
dialogues.challenge: Bend some rules at my base.
dialogues.accept: Then let's bend some bones first! Gently!

lines: Polished emeralds all morning. Then I polished the polishing cloth.
It was looking dull. I couldn't bear it.
dialogues.challenge: Shine for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you sparkle under pressure!

lines: At your base I'll keep the rarest treasures: gems, amethyst, and if you're very lucky, beacons, totems and nether stars.
dialogues.challenge: I'm feeling lucky. Fight me.
dialogues.accept: A gem of a challenge! Let's go!

lines: Piglins. They see gold and lose their minds. And I wear a LOT of gold.
dialogues.challenge: My base has no piglins.
dialogues.accept: Then I'm bringing ALL my gold. Fight me!

lines: Amethyst geodes deep underground. Purple crystals humming in the dark. It's like the world wears jewellery.
If you listen closely. I listen very closely.
dialogues.challenge: I've got geodes near my base.
dialogues.accept: Then let's dig in. To a fight!
dialogues.farewell: They have a lot to say.

lines: The Eternita Stone was cut from the First Dragon's own scales, they say. I'd give anything just to see it.
See it, appraise it, faint a little. In that order.
dialogues.challenge: Help me earn it.
dialogues.accept: Then prove you could hold it!

lines: Spent the morning in the Nether. Lost my eyebrows. Again.
Only my pride. And my eyebrows.
dialogues.challenge: Work for me. After a fight.
dialogues.accept: Things are about to get heated!

lines: At your base I'll stock everything from the Nether: blaze rods, quartz, glowstone, and netherite, if you dare.
Hardest stuff there is. Except my stubbornness.
dialogues.challenge: I dare. Fight me.
dialogues.accept: Then let's forge something!

lines: Ghasts. Big floating crybabies that shoot fire. You'd think I'd be used to them.
Every time one screams, I scream back. It's a whole thing.
dialogues.challenge: No ghasts at my base.
dialogues.accept: Quiet? I'll take it. Fight me!

lines: Crimson forests. Red fungus, glowing vines, the hum of the world's molten heart. It's home.
dialogues.challenge: My base is a bit cooler.
dialogues.accept: I'll survive. After I win!

lines: Y Ddraig Goch made the molten heart of the world, and the Nether is where it still beats loudest.
On quiet nights. It sounds angry. Or hungry. Hard to tell with dragons.
dialogues.challenge: Let's find out together.
dialogues.accept: Then let's light the fire!

lines: Walked to the edge of the world yesterday. Looked over. Nothing looked back.
dialogues.challenge: Walk with me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you can handle the void!

lines: At a base I'll gather what the End offers: pearls, purpur, shulker shells, even elytra.
I can get anything. Coming back is the hard part.
dialogues.challenge: Come back to my base. Fight first.
dialogues.accept: Then let's warp right into it!
dialogues.farewell: The End will wait. It always does.

lines: Shulkers. Little boxes that make you float. I hate floating. I'm a walker, it's in the name.
Voidfloater just doesn't have the same ring.
dialogues.challenge: My base keeps your feet on the ground.
dialogues.accept: Grounded? I'm in. Fight me!

lines: The outer End islands. Purple towers, chorus trees, silence that goes on forever.
Lonely is just peaceful with fewer interruptions.
dialogues.challenge: My base is pretty peaceful.
dialogues.accept: Then let's interrupt it, briefly!

lines: Ouroboros guards the spaces between things. Out past the End, reality gets thin. I've felt it.
Like the world was holding its breath. Waiting for something to fall through.
dialogues.challenge: Let's make sure nothing does.
dialogues.accept: Then prove you're ready for the void!
dialogues.farewell: As safe as nothing can be.

lines: Wrote a ballad about a chicken this morning. It's twelve verses. The chicken left after two.
dialogues.challenge: Play for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: A battle hymn! Let's go!
dialogues.farewell: Verse thirteen is the good one.

lines: At your base I'll play while everyone works, and they'll all work faster. Music's magic, really.
Fifteen percent! I'd go higher but the creatures start dancing instead.
dialogues.challenge: Fifteen percent. Fight me.
dialogues.accept: Then let's make some noise!

lines: Allays. They steal my lute picks. They also hum along off-key.
dialogues.challenge: No allays at my base. Promise.
dialogues.accept: A captive audience? Let's fight!

lines: Flower forests! The bees keep the beat. I just add the melody.
Do the bees like your music?
Nobody's been stung yet. That's a rave review.
dialogues.challenge: My base has flowers and bees.
dialogues.accept: Then let's start the show!

lines: I sing the old songs too: of the twelve Sovereigns, and the Council of Eternita, and the First Dragon's long sleep.
♪ A thousand years asleep, a thousand years awake... ♪ The second verse is about you, if you're brave.
dialogues.challenge: Let's write that verse.
dialogues.accept: Then let's give it a good fight scene!

lines: Changed the sheets, swept the floors, kicked out a sleepwalking cow.
She checked in under a false name.
dialogues.challenge: Keep a bed for me. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: Checking in for a fight? Very well!

lines: At your base I'll keep a bed ready. Sleep through the night and you'll wake with full hearts.
Breakfast costs extra. Hearts are free.
dialogues.challenge: I'll take the hearts. Fight me.
dialogues.accept: Let's see if you've earned a good night's rest!
dialogues.farewell: There's always a room for you.

lines: Phantoms. Every guest who skips sleep brings them. Terrible for business.
I put up signs. Nobody reads signs.
dialogues.challenge: My base follows the rules.
dialogues.accept: A well-rested base! Let's fight!

lines: Snowy taiga. Long nights, warm fires, guests who never want to leave.
dialogues.challenge: My base pays its bills.
dialogues.accept: Then I'll move in. After a fight!

lines: The First Dragon sleeps a thousand years, then wakes a thousand. Imagine the bed you'd need for that.
Constantly. I've drawn plans. It's mostly pillows.
dialogues.challenge: Build it at my base.
dialogues.accept: Then let's fight for the pillows!

lines: My morning: tea, a portrait sitting, and pretending to listen to my advisors.
They talk so much. About so little.
dialogues.challenge: Rule from my base. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: A duel! How delightfully old-fashioned!

lines: At your base my presence attracts... better company. Rare creatures come calling, as they should.
dialogues.challenge: I'd like some quality. Fight me.
dialogues.accept: Then let's see if you're worthy of my company!

lines: Pillagers. Dreadful manners. They never bow, and their crossbows are frightfully common.
dialogues.challenge: My base has manners.
dialogues.accept: How refreshing! A duel, then!

lines: Mushroom fields! No monsters, charming mooshrooms, and absolutely nobody else. Exclusive.
Empty is what exclusive looks like.
dialogues.challenge: My base is very exclusive.
dialogues.accept: Then I insist on a duel at once!

lines: My family claims descent from the Age of Crowns, when kingdoms ruled from coast to coast. We still have the crown. Somewhat dented.
The Age of Ashes was very hard on headwear.
dialogues.challenge: Help me build a new kingdom.
dialogues.accept: A new kingdom? I'm listening. En garde!

lines: Taught a creature to kick this morning. It kicked me. Lesson learned.
dialogues.challenge: Teach at my base. Fight first?
dialogues.accept: A practical lesson! Let's go!

lines: At your base I can teach your creatures new moves, three at a time, for a little XP. Old dogs, new tricks.
Any creature willing to listen. Which is fewer than you'd think.
dialogues.challenge: Teach me something. Fight first.
dialogues.accept: Lesson one: dodge!

lines: Evokers. They summon fangs from the ground. Totally unteachable. Very rude students.
Once. It bit me. With the ground.
dialogues.challenge: My base has well-behaved students.
dialogues.accept: Finally! Let's warm up. On you!

lines: Windswept hills! Wind in your hair, steep slopes, perfect for practising balance.
Falling is just balance practice with extra steps.
dialogues.challenge: My base has hills to train on.
dialogues.accept: Then let's start training!

lines: Every move I teach comes from one of the twelve influences. Fire from Y Ddraig Goch, frost from the Hrimwyrm, and so on. I'm just the messenger.
dialogues.challenge: Teach me their secrets.
dialogues.accept: Then let's start with the basics: combat!
